headline: UnitedHealth Group says AI tools have cut the time its clinicians spend reviewing patient charts by 33% and shortened its appeals process by 26%.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a very large US insurer and care provider gives specific AI results on an earnings call, though they are company claims and not independently checked.
importance_line: Patients of UnitedHealth's employed doctors may see them spend less time on records and more with patients, and members face AI plan recommendations, but the figures are the company's own and lawmakers are separately moving to limit AI in claim decisions.
summary: PYMNTS reports that on UnitedHealth Group's third-quarter earnings call on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026, chief executive Steve Hemsley said AI-enabled chart summarization (software that condenses a patient's medical record for the doctor), now offered to more than 40% of the insurer's employed clinicians, has cut chart review time by 33%, and that AI-assisted research has shortened appeal cycles by 26%. These are the company's own figures; PYMNTS adds that US lawmakers have proposed the Doctors Not AI Act, which would stop an automated system from having the final say on whether an insurer approves a claim.
notes: Full PYMNTS text read. Percentages are company claims from the earnings call. The article does not say what kind of appeals are meant, so the entry says only 'appeals' and 'appeal cycles'.
